quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track, moving in either direction. Do not stop your vehicle on the tracks. Make sure your entire vehicle clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Okay if you do not know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other cars and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing yellow light, slow down and go carefully. You do not need to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: You should stay farther back when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see directly behind their vehicle.
A small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see directly behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers cannot see you directly behind them. Stay farther back. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so increase your distance to see around them.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, turn your wheels toward the edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car rolls away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so your car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet pavement. Slow down when the road is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot:

options.text: Turn on your reverse lights.
Make sure drivers coming from any direction can see your vehicle.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers coming from any direction can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your parked car is not a hazard. Wherever you park, make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes sudden steering while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction keeps you from seeing and hearing warning signs of danger.

questions.question: If a driver aged 16 or 17 is convicted of using an electronic device while driving, what happens?

options.text: A $500 fine.
A 10-day license suspension.
A 30-day license suspension.

questions.correctAnswerText: A 30-day license suspension.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot use a cell phone or electronic device while driving. If a 16- or 17-year-old is convicted, they must take a driver retraining course. If they get another moving violation within three years of finishing the course, their license will be suspended for at least 30 days.

questions.question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students have left the bus.
The stop arm goes back in.
The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights and extends its stop arm, you must stay completely stopped. Keep stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm retracts, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: What do defensive drivers think about?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
They expect nothing and give nothing to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and get ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you expect mistakes from other drivers and prepare to handle them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign shows a hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, how can you help other drivers see you?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Always use your low beam headlights when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean about passing?

options.text: You can pass after you see the sign.
You can pass if it seems safe.
You cannot pass under any circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign is a rule you must follow. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: What danger occurs when you drive too fast on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires will slide over the water.
You will lose the ability to judge speed and control.
Water from your tires will block other drivers' vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires will slide over the water.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, tires have good grip at speeds up to about 35 mph. When you go faster, your tires may ride on the water like water skis. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus picks up or drops off passengers, you must come to a complete stop before reaching the bus. This applies no matter what direction you are traveling.

questions.question: How are stopping distances and crash severity affected by vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean about passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic travels in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive very close to parked cars to leave more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Leave space between your car and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their car without knowing you are there.

questions.question: Which of these is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: On cold, wet days, shaded spots on roads can freeze over. Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw after other parts.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and move forward carefully.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass cars that seem stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or enter your path, or where one line of traffic meets another, look left and right along your vehicle to make sure no one is coming.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when it is safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop like you would on other roads. Use the merging lane to speed up and smoothly join the fast-moving traffic already on the highway.

questions.question: Pressing the brakes hard on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and make you lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid hard braking.
